overview: This bill creates the Finger Lakes National Heritage Area in upstate New York, covering 14 counties including Monroe, Onondaga, Tompkins, and Seneca. A national heritage area is a region recognized for its history, culture, and landscape, where a local organization works with the National Park Service to promote and preserve those resources; the land stays in private or local hands. The Finger Lakes Tourism Alliance would serve as the local managing group and must submit a management plan to the Interior Department within three years. Federal assistance for the area would end 15 years after the bill becomes law. As of September 17, 2026, a Senate committee had approved it and it was placed on the Senate calendar for possible floor action.
for: Supporters say the designation would bring national recognition and modest federal support to a region rich in history and natural beauty, boosting tourism and local preservation efforts.
against: Critics say heritage areas add to ongoing federal costs at a time when the National Park Service has a large maintenance backlog, and that promoting regional tourism is better handled locally.
